analysis:
All eight units are test or fixture changes. I found no executable production behavior and no concrete security regression. Files examined: ClusterRuntimeApprovalFactsTests.swift (head lines 375-901), the new glm-5.3-flash-dev-branch17.json fixture, and ClusterApprovalFixture.swift (patch plus base).

The tests exercise the declared public-model path: ClusterPublicModels.declared, parity qualifications, pair serving grants, and release candidate selection. They assert the following:
- Grants for declared models carry the evidence document's SHA-256, and the checked-in report digest must match it (line 413-414).
- Candidates whose catalog entry is not their own are refused (lines 598-613).
- Undeclared models fall back to record-derived grants only.
- Pipeline qualifications are omitted when the config lacks a usable num_hidden_layers, and the facts report this.
- Models the build does not list are never described.
- A divergence record contradicts a pass record of the same shape.
These assertions are mostly security-positive: they check fail-closed behavior.

The fixture contains no secrets. Its content is only digests, a Metal library class, and qualification metadata.

Questions the integration pass should check against production code outside this batch, since the tests assert behavior I could not see:
1. Test line 579-580 asserts that a declared model's grant is its declared families whatever the records say, even when there are none or when they diverge. If production implements this, qualification for declared models rests on a source-hardcoded declaration plus an evidence digest, rather than on the passing records. The evidence digest is checked against the repository report only in tests (lines 413-414). A review should confirm that the production declaration and its evidence are release-reviewed, and that the coordinator treats a grant as bounded by the build qualification (A-017, T-054).
2. The declared request envelope is 1,048,576 prompt and output tokens with tools and sampling, and an image or video flag follows the catalog modalities. The production resource and DoS limits for these values (T-010) are not visible here.
The base files for the test and fixture files were not fully supplied, and the patch excerpts are truncated, so I could not verify those parts.
